questions.question: A and B ran a race of 3600 meters on a 600-meter circular track. They meet at starting point for the first time 15 minutes after the start of the race. Find the time (in minutes) taken by B to complete the race. If he runs at half of the speed of A.
questions.questionHtml: A and B ran a race of 3600 meters on a 600-meter circular track. They meet at starting point for the first time 15 minutes after the start of the race. Find the time (in minutes) taken by B to complete the race. If he runs at half of the speed of A.
questions.solution:
Given that:

Length of circular path = 600 meters

Speed of B = 1/2 of the speed of A.

Formula Used 

Time = Distance/Speed

Calculation

Let the speed of A is 2x and speed of B is x .

According to question,

600/( 2x – x ) = 15 min

⇒ x = 40 meter/min

So, the speed of B = 40 meter/ min

Time taken by B to complete the race = D/S = 3600/40

⇒ 90 minutes

∴ The time taken by B to complete the race is 90 minutes.

questions.question: A car and a bus were both travelling in the same direction. At 7.30 a.m., the car, moving at 72 km/h, was 4.2 kilometres behind the bus. The car was 15.8 kilometres ahead of the bus at 8:15 a.m. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to that of the bus?
questions.questionHtml: A car and a bus were both travelling in the same direction. At 7.30 a.m., the car, moving at 72 km/h, was 4.2 kilometres behind the bus. The car was 15.8 kilometres ahead of the bus at 8:15 a.m. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to that of the bus?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Speed of car = 72 km/h

Distance covered by car in 1 hour i.e. 60 minutes = 72 km

Distance covered by car in 45 minutes (from 7 : 30 a.m to 8 : 15 a.m) = 54 km [i.e. (72/60) × 45]

Distance covered by bus in 45 minutes = (54 - 4.2 - 15.8) km = 34 km

When time is constant then,

The speed of the car ∶ The Speed of the Bus = Distance covered by car ∶ Distance covered by bus in 45 minutes = 54 ∶ 34

27 ∶ 17

questions.question: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
questions.questionHtml: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a train crossing two objects in the same direction:

Speed of Train (V) = (S2 × T2 − S1 × T1) ÷ (T2 − T1)

V = (6 × 14 − 4 × 12) ÷ (14 − 12)

V = (84 − 48) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of person 1 (v1) = 4 km/h | Time (t1) = 12 s

Speed of person 2 (v2) = 6 km/h | Time (t2) = 14 s

Let the speed of the train be V km/h and the length of the train be L meters.

Formula Used:

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Length of train (L) is constant in both cases.

⇒ L = (V − 4) × (5/18) × 12 — (i)

⇒ L = (V − 6) × (5/18) × 14 — (ii)

Equating (i) and (ii):

⇒ (V − 4) × 12 = (V − 6) × 14

⇒ 12V − 48 = 14V − 84

⇒ 14V − 12V = 84 − 48

⇒ 2V = 36

⇒ V = 18 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = V1 − V2. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed = V1 + V2.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a pole, person, or tree, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train.

questions.question: The speeds of train A and train B are 46.8 km/h and 61.2 km/h, respectively. The lengths of A and B are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5. When running in the opposite direction. They cross each other completely in 12 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will train B take to cross a 336 m long tunnel?
questions.questionHtml: The speeds of train A and train B are 46.8 km/h and 61.2 km/h, respectively. The lengths of A and B are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5. When running in the opposite direction. They cross each other completely in 12 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will train B take to cross a 336 m long tunnel?
questions.solution:
Given:

The speeds of train A and train B are 46.8 km/h and 61.2 km/h, respectively.

The lengths of A and B are in the ratio 3 ∶ 5

Concept used:

Time = Distance/speed

km/h × (5/18) = m/sec

Relative Speed of 2 bodies:

Sum of their individual speeds if they are moving in the opposite direction

If a train cross another tunnel it will cross length of the tunnel + its own length

Calculation:

Relative speed of the two trains running in the opposite direction = 46.8 + 61.2 = 108 km/h

⇒ 108 km/h

Speed in m/sec = 108 × (5/18)

⇒ 30 m/sec

So, total distance covered = 12 × 30

⇒ 360 m

Let the length of train A and B be 3x and 5x

So, 3x + 5x = 8x

Here,

8x = 360

⇒ x = 360/8 = 45

So, The length of train B = 5x (Given)

⇒ 5x = 45 × 5 = 225

The length of train B = 225 m

Now,

Time = \(\frac{225 + 336}{61.2 \times \frac{5}{18}}\)

⇒ \(\frac{561}{17}\)

⇒ 33 sec

∴ Required time is 33 sec.

questions.question: X & Y are two ports 780 km apart. A boat starts from X at 10:00 pm and travel towards Y at 130 km/h. Another boat starts from Y at 11:00 pm and travels towards X at 70 km/h. At what time do they meet?
questions.questionHtml: X & Y are two ports 780 km apart. A boat starts from X at 10:00 pm and travel towards Y at 130 km/h. Another boat starts from Y at 11:00 pm and travels towards X at 70 km/h. At what time do they meet?
questions.solution:
Given:

X & Y are two ports 780 km apart.

A boat starts from X at 10:00 pm and travels towards Y at 130 km/h. Another boat starts from Y at 11:00 pm and travels towards X at 70 km/h. 

Concept used:

Relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds while two bodies are coming from the opposite direction.

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Let boat A start at 10.00 PM from port X and boat B start at 11.00 PM from port Y.

Let boat A be at point M at 11.00 PM when boat B starts from port Y.

XM = 130 km (∵ Speed of boat X = 130 km per hour)

So, MY = XY - XM

⇒ MY = 780 - 130

⇒ MY = 650

Relative speed = 130 + 70 = 200 kmph

Time taken to meet each each

⇒ 650/200

⇒ 3.25 hours

⇒ 3 hours 0.25 × 60 minutes

⇒ 3 hours 15 minutes

Now, they will meet at

⇒ 11.00 PM + 3 hours 15 minutes

⇒ 02.15 AM

∴ They will meet at 02.15 AM.

questions.question: A policeman saw a thief at a distance of 800m. When the policeman started chasing the thief, the thief started running. If the ratio of the speeds of the policeman to the thief is 3:2, then the distance travelled by the policeman to catch the thief is
questions.questionHtml: A policeman saw a thief at a distance of 800m. When the policeman started chasing the thief, the thief started running. If the ratio of the speeds of the policeman to the thief is 3:2, then the distance travelled by the policeman to catch the thief is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the time of the chase is constant for both the policeman and the thief, Distance is directly proportional to Speed.

Ratio of Speeds (Policeman : Thief) = 3 : 2 ⇒ Ratio of Distances = 3 : 2.

Difference in distance units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = 800 m.

Total distance traveled by the policeman = 3 units = 3 × 800 m = 2400 m = 2.4 km.

∴ The correct answer is 2.4 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial distance between Policeman and Thief = 800 m.

Ratio of speed of Policeman (Vp) to Thief (Vt) = 3 : 2.

Calculations:

Let the speed of the policeman be 3x and the speed of the thief be 2x.

⇒ Relative speed in same direction = 3x − 2x = x.

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Initial Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time (T) = 800 ÷ x

⇒ Distance covered by the policeman = Speed of policeman × Time

⇒ Distance = 3x × (800 ÷ x)

⇒ Distance = 3 × 800 = 2400 m

⇒ Distance in km = 2400 ÷ 1000 = 2.4 km

∴ The correct answer is 2.4 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference between their speeds: (u − v).

Distance and Speed Relation

When time is constant, the ratio of distances covered is directly proportional to the ratio of speeds (D1/D2 = S1/S2).

Unit Conversion

To convert meters to kilometers, divide the value by 1000 (1 km = 1000 m).

questions.question: Two trains running in opposite directions cross a man standing on the platform in 30 sec and 15 sec respectively and they cross each other in 25 sec. The ratio of their speeds is:
questions.questionHtml: Two trains running in opposite directions cross a man standing on the platform in 30 sec and 15 sec respectively and they cross each other in 25 sec. The ratio of their speeds is:
questions.solution:
The speed of the first train and the second train be "a" and "b"

Length of the first train = 30a and Length of the second train = 15b

⇒ 25 = \(\frac {30a + 15b}{a + b}\) ⇒ 25a + 25b = 30a + 15b ⇒ 10b = 5a

⇒ a/b = 10/5 = 2/1 ⇒ a : b = 2 : 1

questions.question: A train of 150 meters crosses a bridge of 300 meters in 30 seconds. In how much time will this train cross a second train coming from the opposite direction having a length of 200 meters and running at a speed of 36 km/h?
questions.questionHtml: A train of 150 meters crosses a bridge of 300 meters in 30 seconds. In how much time will this train cross a second train coming from the opposite direction having a length of 200 meters and running at a speed of 36 km/h?
questions.solution:
The total distance that the first train needs to cover to cross the bridge is:

150 meters (length of train) + 300 meters (length of bridge) = 450 meters.

So, the speed of the first train is:

Speed = Distance/Time = 450/30 = 15 m/s

The speed of the second train in meters per second:

Speed = 36 km/h = (36 * 1000)/3600 = 10 m/s

Since the second train is coming from the opposite direction, the relative speed between the two trains will be the sum of their speeds:

Relative speed = Speed of first train + Speed of second train
= 15 + 10 = 25 m/s

To cross each other, the length of both trains will be covered, which is 150 m + 200 m = 350 m.

The time taken for the two trains to cross each other is:

Time = Distance/Relative speed = 350/25 = 14 seconds

questions.question: In a race of 500m, A can beat B by 50m. In a race of 450m, B beats C by 50m. By how many metres will A beat C in a race of 1500 m?
questions.questionHtml: In a race of 500m, A can beat B by 50m. In a race of 450m, B beats C by 50m. By how many metres will A beat C in a race of 1500 m?
questions.solution:
In a race of 500m, A beats B by 50m

⇒ A : B = 500 : 450

In a race of 450m, B beats C by 50m

⇒ B : C = 450 : 400

Now,

\(\frac{A}{C} = \;\frac{A}{B} \times \frac{B}{C}\)

\( \Rightarrow \frac{A}{C} = \;\frac{{500}}{{450}} \times \frac{{450}}{{400}}\)

\( \Rightarrow \frac{A}{C} = \;\frac{5}{4}\)

⇒ When A covers 5m, C covers 4m.

⇒ When A covers 1500m, C will cover \(\frac{4}{5} \times 1500 = 1200m\)

∴ In a race of 1500m, A beats C by (1500 - 1200) = 300m.

questions.question: A car crosses a man moving along a road at 6 km/hr. The man could see the car up to 2 minutes. Find the speed of the car, if at the time of disappearance of the car, the distance of the car to man was 1.2 km.
questions.questionHtml: A car crosses a man moving along a road at 6 km/hr. The man could see the car up to 2 minutes. Find the speed of the car, if at the time of disappearance of the car, the distance of the car to man was 1.2 km.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative Speed = 1.2 km ÷ (2/60) hr = 1.2 × 30 = 36 km/hr

Since the car and man move in the same direction:

Speed of car = Relative Speed + Speed of man = 36 + 6 = 42 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 42 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of the man (Vm) = 6 km/hr

Time of visibility (t) = 2 minutes = 2/60 hr = 1/30 hr

Relative distance at disappearance (d) = 1.2 km

Formula:

Relative Speed (Vrel) = Distance / Time

When moving in the same direction, Vrel = Vcar − Vman

Calculations:

⇒ Vrel = 1.2 km ÷ (1/30) hr

⇒ Vrel = 1.2 × 30 = 36 km/hr

⇒ Vcar − 6 = 36

⇒ Vcar = 36 + 6

⇒ Vcar = 42 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 42 km/hr.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

For objects moving in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference (V1 − V2). For objects moving in opposite directions, it is the sum (V1 + V2).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Visibility Problems

In fog or visibility questions, the distance of disappearance represents the relative distance covered by the faster object during the given time interval.
